hypothesis: The load-use hazard is being resolved by DISCARDING the dependent instruction instead of holding and replaying it. When a load is in EX (id_ex_mem_read) and a younger instruction in ID consumes its destination, if_stage's stall path drives if_id_valid<=0 (identical to the redirect/flush path), so the dependent instruction that should be held in IF/ID is replaced by a bubble and is never re-fetched (PC had already advanced to dependent+4, so it is permanently lost). Because id_stage has no stall input, the only way the current design injects the EX bubble is by invalidating if_id, which is exactly what destroys the dependent. The result is that the consuming instruction never executes and its target register simply retains its pre-load (stale) value: t07_load_use x3 stays 0 (expected 0x2468acf0), x8 stays 0xde (expected 0), x13 stays 0x1 (expected 0x8001). The same mechanism explains t08_store_fwd being uniformly off by one: the program does `lw x,mem; addi x,x,1; sw x,...`; the addi is the lost load-use dependent, so x keeps its pre-load value (one less than the expected loaded+1) and the store writes that stale, off-by-one value into x7/x8/x9/x11 and DMEM[0x210..0x218] (0xa5a5a5ab vs 0xa5a5a5aa, 0x7ab vs 0x7aa, etc.). This is the deliberate anti-pattern the spec forbids ('never clear a valid instruction because of a stall'); the datapath itself is now correct, which is why bench_ooo_overlap64 passes 1943/1943 with the right exit code and only the two hazard-specific suites f
constraints: During load_use_stall: PC must hold, if_id_valid must STAY 1 and if_id_pc/if_id_pc_plus4/if_id_instr must HOLD their current values (the dependent instruction must be preserved, never cleared).

Exactly one bubble must be injected into ID/EX on the stall cycle (id_ex_valid=0 for that edge); the held dependent must advance into ID/EX on the following cycle. Adding an internal stall input to id_stage (or equivalent replay control) is

load_use_stall detection must remain: id_ex_valid && id_ex_mem_read && (id_ex_rd_addr!=0) && id_valid && ((id_rs1_used && id_rs1_addr==id_ex_rd_addr) || (id_rs2_used && id_rs2_addr==id_ex_rd_addr)); confirm id_rs2_used is asserted for store
Store-rs2 data dependency must be resolved either by an extra EX stall or by MEM/WB->EX forwarding of the store data; do not write stale store wdata.
Control-flow redirect MUST still take priority over stall: on redirect flush both IF/ID and ID/EX; do not hold a valid instruction across a redirect.
Top-level and per-module port names/widths are frozen (only internal signals may be added); module boundaries unchanged.
Synchronous active-low reset; dmem_valid = mem_dmem_valid & rst_n & ~halted; once halted freeze PC fetch and stop retiring new instructions.
Do not touch teacher TB, spec, or scoring scripts; no test-vector hardcoding.
